messages.subject: Re: Can we customize the ticks(orientation, length, etc) in ggplot, just like using 'mgp = c( , , )' in normal plot function?
parts:
On Wed, Aug 31, 2011 at 8:38 PM, Zhenjiang Lan <lan.zh...@gmail.com> wrote:
> #here's the example:
> y<-sample(1:20)
> x<-1:20
> plot(x,y,xlim=c(0,20),ylim=c(0,20),xaxs="r",yaxs="r")
> #this plot can also generated by qplot:
> qplot(x,y,xlim=c(0,20),ylim=c(0,20))

> #then we can modify the plot by:
> plot(x,y,xlim=c(0,20),ylim=c(0,20),xaxs="i",yaxs="i")
> #how can we get the same result in ggplot2?

ggplot(dd, aes(x, y)) + geom_point() +
scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(0, 20)) +
scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), limits = c(0, 20))

but notice this is not good practice because the two points on the
boundary of the plot region are clipped. You want some margin. Here's
an example of a fixed margin whose size is determined by the user:

ggplot(dd, aes(x, y)) + geom_point() +
scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0.2), limits = c(0, 20)) +
scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0.2), limits = c(0, 20))

The first value in expand = is a multiplicative factor for the margin,
which is 0.05 by default; the second value is an additive constant.

> #we can also change the ticks' orientation:
> plot(x,y,xlim=c(0,20),ylim=c(0,20),tcl=0.3)
> #even like this:
> plot(x,y,xlim=c(0,20),ylim=c(0,20),tcl=0.3,mgp=c(1,-2,0))
> #how can we realize these in ggplot2?

I imagine that if you played around in grid graphics long enough, you
could find some way to do it, but I wouldn't touch that request with a
10-foot pole. Within the set of opts() available in ggplot2, it can't
be done easily, if at all, and I'm pretty certain that's a designed
feature (hint).

HTH,
Dennis
